column1: # measured_claims.tsv — claims this repository makes about itself that can be re-derived.
# Four tab-separated columns:
#   id            stable name, used by the baseline file
#   description   what the claim says, in words
#   claim_cmd     prints the CLAIMED value, read out of a committed file
#   measure_cmd   prints the MEASURED value, derived from the tree
#   fix_cmd       the ONE command that repairs a drift, printed when it drifts
# A row belongs here only if `measure_cmd` re-derives the number from the tree.
# That is the whole admission rule. Prose is out of scope: a claim nobody can
# re-run is a claim this gate cannot check, and pretending otherwise would make
# the gate the very thing it exists to catch.
# Both commands run from the repository root with `set -o pipefail`. Emit one
# bare value and nothing else; leading and trailing whitespace is stripped.
# fix_cmd is not run by the gate -- it is printed. A drift message that says
# "regenerate the file that holds it" sends the reader looking for which file
# and which flag; on 2026-08-28 seven pull requests and three agents each paid
# that search separately. Naming the command is the difference between a gate
# that reports a problem and one that hands you the fix.
id
gate_ratchet_list_pair
column2: the unnamed-gate ratchet count matches the list it summarises

column1: witness_census_sha256
column2: the sabotage census corpus digest matches the run-pass corpus content, naming and order
column4: find tests/run-pass -name '*.sio' -type f | LC_ALL=C sort | tr '\n' '\0' | xargs -0 sha256sum | (sha256sum 2>/dev/null || shasum -a 256) | awk '{print $1}'

column1: dce_chain_exit_code
column2: the //@ exit-code header on the DCE chain fixture matches what its binary returns
column4: T=$(mktemp); SOUNIO_SOUC_ENGINE=lean_single bash bin/souc compile tests/multimodule/dce_reach/dce_chain_main.sio -o "$T" >/dev/null 2>&1 && { chmod +x "$T"; "$T" >/dev/null 2>&1; echo $?; }; rm -f "$T"
column5: bash scripts/ci/madaros_dce_reachability_gate.sh   # authoritative check: it pins the same numbers by hand. If it passes, the //@ exit-code header is the stale side; if it fails, the binary changed.
